structure:
repos/trade-imports-animals-frontend (on main) is the live-animals import notification frontend: a Hapi and Nunjucks service whose pages come from a set-agnostic journey platform under src/server/app/ plus one set, src/server/app/sets/live-animals/. The set holds four things. (1) journeys/linear/features/: 19 feature folders, each one page or a small group of pages, with page.js (id, slug, collects, maturity), controller.js (routes and handlers), template.njk, validate.js, a copy/ folder of copy.en.js and copy.cy.js, and a co-located Playwright fit spec; the bigger features (commodities, transport, addresses, documents, check-answers) hold sub-page folders and a fit/ folder. (2) journeys/linear/flow/: the 8 journey sections and their page order (start, about-the-consignment, description-of-the-goods, transport-and-arrival, documents, consignment-parties, contact-address, review, the last gated on readyForCheckYourAnswers), task rows and row status, the entry guard, and section captions with their own copy. (3) obligations/: index.js and 11 section files saying which answers are in scope, mandatory and at what cardinality. (4) services/commodities/: the commodity reference client, its rules and its stub. src/server/app/routes-live-animals.js mounts the set as a Hapi plugin and takes its route list from features/index.js, which composes 28 controller route bundles; src/server/app/flow/ holds the generic dispatch, gates, prerequisites and navigation the set configures. src/server/app/shared/ (23 files, about 1,100 lines of source) holds the layout, the kit, the Save and continue and Save and return buttons, the trail, the error summary and the service-wide copy; src/server/app/page-maturity/ renders a maturity banner; src/server/common/components/ holds the accessible-autocomplete and multi-select-search macros and READMEs, and src/client/ their client-side JavaScript plus the service's custom SCSS (notification list, pagination, date picker, commodity total, summary-card error, task list, icon button). Two decision ledgers exist: src/server/app/docs/decisions.md (platform architecture decisions, 8 headings) and src/server/app/sets/live-animals/docs/page-design.md (788 lines, a per-page design-decision record under 15 page headings), beside journey-flow-and-gates.md (297 lines), features.md, limits.md, obligation-model.md and copy-status.md. Fit specs sit both inside the features (22 *.fit.spec.js files, about 16,200 lines) and at the repo root (fit/live-animals-journey.js, 1,910 lines, which drives the whole happy path page by page, and fit/journey-smoke.fit.spec.js). The scoped source comes to roughly 41,000 lines, cut here into 19 parts. What the scope leaves out, and so stays unclaimed: the roughly 30,000 lines of co-located *.test.js unit tests, which the scope does not name; the platform layers it does not name (engine/, bridge/, model/, lib/, analysis/, auth/, services/ other than the set's own commodity service, and the persistence and session records); journeys/linear/fixtures/ (characterisation-oracles.json, a 65 KB generated test oracle); and the how-to recipes under both docs/ folders (add-a-page.md, add-a-field.md, add-a-section.md, add-a-collection.md, architecture.md, testing.md, test-ownership.md, services.md, persistence.md, validation.md, scope-and-wipe.md, engine.md, cardinality.md, analysis.md, lighthouse.md), which say how to change the code rather than what it does today. There is no machine-readable rulings ledger such as spec/decisions.json; the two markdown ledgers above are what the repo keeps. Welsh copy (copy.cy.js) is read for key parity with the English file rather than claimed string by string.

Extracted in 19 parts:
Part 1, Set wiring, journey flow and obligations: Part 1 read how the live-animals set is mounted and sequenced, not what its pages say. It read in full: src/server/app/routes.js and routes-live-animals.js (the Hapi plugin that mounts the set and the order it configures its seams in); the generic flow layer src/server/app/flow/ (dispatch.js, gates.js, prerequisites.js, navigation.js, journey-flow.js, section-status.js); the set's identity sets/live-animals/set.js and its journey config journeys/linear/config.js; the composition files journeys/linear/features/index.js (28 route bundles, 15 dispatch pages), features/evaluation.js and features/system/evaluation.js; the whole of journeys/linear/flow/ (flow.js's 8 sections, task-rows.js's 12 rows, entry-guard.js, stored-answers.js, notification-action-slugs.js, section-captions/index.js with copy.en.js and copy.cy.js, fixtures/happy-path.json, and reachability-fixtures/seeds.js, scope-states.js and enumerate-answer-states.js); all 12 obligation files (obligations/index.js plus the 11 section files, commodities/identifiers.js, lines.js and aggregates.js among them); the eight files of sets/live-animals/services/commodities/; and the two test-support files (sets/live-animals/test-support.js, journeys/linear/test-support.js). To ground facts those files rest on it also read, outside its own list: shared/paths.js (the URL builders), bridge/obligation-source.js (SYSTEM_POPULATED, ENFORCED_AT_CONTINUE), bridge/status/index.js and bridge/status/vocabulary.js (statusOf and the five statuses), the seven gate helpers under model/obligations/helpers/, obligation-purity.js and set-completeness.js (the boot assertions), each dispatch page's `collects` from its controller.js and each flow page's id, slug, subPage and maturity from its page.js, shared/kit.js's CYA_SLUG and CANCEL_AMEND_SLUG, features/transport/transporter-add-session.js and features/commodities/search/selection/rows.js (the flow-only key values), services/reference-data/request.js, common/services/mode.js and common/helpers/frontend-url.js. It covers: the set base, id and the URL shape every page hangs off; the 28 route bundles and which pages the flow holds that declare no obligations; how a page claims an obligation and how a derived page or section gate is worked out; the 8 journey sections in order with their pages and the review section's gate; all 12 task rows with their parts, conditions and how rowStatus decides; the two answers enforced at Save and continue and where a trader lands without them; the entry guard and the INS type-question URL; the 9 section captions verbatim in English with Welsh key parity; the 6 flow-only keys; all 52 obligations with their level, mandate, scope condition and cardinality; and the commodity reference service with its code lists, species check and stub. It claims no page's own heading, caption position, fields, hints, options or error messages: each feature's part does that.
Part 2, Shared layout, shared copy and the search components: Part 2 read, in full, the 15 named files of src/server/app/shared/ (layout.njk, kit.js, save-actions.njk, error-summary.njk, error.njk, section-caption.njk, render-macro.js, copy.js, copy.en.js, copy.cy.js, copy-leaves.js, paths.js, paging.js, trail.js, set-context.js), the six files of src/server/app/page-maturity/ (banner.njk, levels.js, page-maturity.js, _banner.scss and the English and Welsh copy), both shared search components under src/server/common/components/ (accessible-autocomplete and multi-select-search, each with macro.njk, its SCSS and its README), the client bundle (src/client/javascripts/application.js and its six component modules: accessible-autocomplete, autocomplete-text, multi-select-search, transporter-filter, region-code-prefix, status-announcer), the three client helpers (search-fold, bold-matches, welsh-results-available), the SCSS entry application.scss with its two core partials, seven component partials and two helper partials, and the type-ahead FIT spec src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/type-ahead.fit.spec.js. It covered the chrome every page shares rather than any one page: the GOV.UK page template the service extends, the service name, header, Alpha phase banner, service navigation and footer, the page-title and section-caption patterns, the Back link and the `from` trail it follows, the Save and continue / Save and return to overview / Cancel and return to overview controls, the error summary and inline field errors, the recoverable-error, stale-action and success banners, the journey status strip, the page-maturity banner and its four levels, every key of the shared English copy module with a parity claim for the Welsh one, the two shared search components with their client-side JavaScript, announcements and SCSS, each custom SCSS partial and the GOV.UK component it extends, the shared paging helper, the set-mounted URL shapes, and every behaviour the type-ahead FIT spec proves with JavaScript on and off. Two files outside the slice are named only where a file read here depends on them: the submitted-search macro the multi-select-search macro imports, and src/config/config.js for the maturity banner's switch. Welsh copy was read for key parity, not claimed string by string.
Part 3, The fit journey driver and the cross-page fit specs: Part 3 read the animals frontend's repo-root fit suite and the three cross-page fit specs in full: fit/live-animals-journey.js (1,910 lines, the shared driver every fit spec imports), fit/journey-smoke.fit.spec.js (366 lines, 9 tests in one describe, 'live-animals journey glue'), fit/sign-in.js (9 lines), playwright.config.js (76 lines), and src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/section-caption.fit.spec.js (5 tests), page-title.fit.spec.js (2 tests) and service-navigation.fit.spec.js (7 tests). The driver has three layers: generic page helpers (axe, overflow, computed-style probes, error summary, Back link, date picker, grid columns, journey form, save-control shape assertions), per-page answer helpers that fill one page and assert the page Save and continue opens (a LANDINGS table of slug and heading for 12 landings), and whole-journey helpers (startNotificationAtOrigin, startNotification, completeAnswerSections, submitCompleteNotification, amendFromList). Values come from src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/fixtures/happy-path.json, read here for the values the driver fills, and species rows from the commodities search test-support module. Covered: the happy path page by page with its URLs, fields, options, buttons and values; sign-in through the stub-auth route; the suite's own set-up (two Playwright projects, base URL, stub-mode web server, no seed step); what each of the 9 smoke tests asserts and that the suite stops at the draft notification view without declaring; the section caption rule and the one page it exempts; the page title rule; and the service navigation items, highlighting and destinations. Not claimed here, because the partition gives them to the feature parts: each page's own copy, hints, validation messages and per-page save-control shape, which this part records only as the rule the driver's shared helpers hold a page to.
Part 4, The notification list (dashboard): Part 4, the notification list (dashboard) of the live-animals set in repos/trade-imports-animals-frontend. Read in full: features/dashboard/page.js (5 lines: id 'dashboard', empty slug, maturity 'exploring'), controller.js (202 lines: renderDashboard plus four routes — GET the list at the set base, POST amend, POST create, GET /start), template.njk (157 lines: amend-refused banner, caption, h1, intro, start-button form, 'Your notifications' h2, a one-third filter aside holding the GET search form, a two-thirds column holding the results label, the GET sort form, one govuk-summary-card per notification with three rows of three cells and an action list, the empty text, and govukPagination), notification-helper.js (158 lines: the sort options and default, date display, commodity label, page-number clamping, the list query string, the pagination links and the results-range label), copy/copy.en.js and copy/copy.cy.js (61 lines each, key for key), view-model/sort-options.js (localised sort option text by index), view-model/row/index.js (toRow), view-model/row/actions.js (74 lines: the per-status action lists), dashboard.fit.spec.js (460 lines, 16 Playwright tests in 6 describes: empty state and start, rows and actions, reference search, pagination, the shared alpha phase banner, accessibility, and the amend-refused banner), and flow/notification-action-slugs.js (amend, cancel-amend, copy, delete). Read for provenance only, as they belong to other parts: shared/paths.js (the set base /live-animals and the route paths), shared/kit.js (routeOptions, surfaces, the status tag map, CYA_SLUG), shared/copy.en.js (the shared 'Copy as new', 'Delete' and status words), shared/paging.js (pageAskedFor and previousAndNextLinks), shared/trail.js (TRAIL_START), shared/layout.njk (where the success and recoverable-error banners render), flow/section-captions (the 'Dashboard' caption), engine/journey.js (listKnownJourneys) and sets/live-animals/set.js (SET_BASE). Covered: the list route and how a trader reaches it; its caption, heading and intro; the start control and both ways of opening a new notification; every cell of a row and the words of every status tag; every row action per status, verbatim, with where it leads; the keyword-or-reference search; the four sort options, the default and how sort is carried; the 20-row page size, the Previous/Next pagination and the results-range wording; the empty state; the amend-refused, notification-deleted and recoverable-error banners; every behaviour the dashboard fit spec proves; and the mechanisms in notification-helper.js and the row view model that reshape a backend notification into a row. It stops at the pages the row actions lead to (overview, notification view, delete, cancel-amend), which belong to their own parts.
Part 5, The overview task list and the notification actions: Part 5, the overview task list and the notification actions, read eleven files of repos/trade-imports-animals-frontend in full: the hub feature folder (page.js, controller.js, template.njk, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js, hub.fit.spec.js, 538 lines), the notification-actions feature folder (page.js, controller.js, notification-actions.fit.spec.js), and two live-animals flow files (flow/task-rows.js, flow/notification-action-slugs.js). Supporting reads for route and constant values only, not claimed beyond what the slice shows: src/server/app/shared/paths.js (hubRoutePath, pageRoutePath, pagePath, hubPath, dashboardPath), src/server/app/shared/trail.js:12-16 (TRAIL_START.overview is 'overview', so the trail parameter reads ?from=overview), src/server/app/shared/kit.js:71 (CANCEL_AMEND_SLUG is 'cancel-amend'), src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/delete-notification/page.js:3 (slug 'delete'), features/check-answers/page.js:3 (slug 'notification-view') and features/check-answers/controller.js:258 (its only registered route), and shared/copy.en.js:51-64 for the shared button strings the two fit specs drive. The part covers one page, the overview at GET /notifications/{journeyId} (its H1 'Overview', the 'Your commodities' totals section, the 'Notification task list' of six numbered section groups holding twelve task rows, and the Review and submit / Return to dashboard button pair), the twelve task rows' titles, hint, link targets and the two status words a row can show, every behaviour the 23 hub fit tests prove, the four notification action slugs (amend, cancel-amend, copy, delete) of which this feature registers only POST /notifications/{journeyId}/copy, that route's success, no-copy, recoverable-failure and stale-token outcomes, the four notification-actions fit tests, and Welsh key parity for the hub's copy. It stops before the confirmation pages the actions lead to (part 7), the dashboard that renders the Copy as new button, the check-answers review page, and the generic flow, gate and status layers under src/server/app/flow and src/server/app/bridge.
Part 6, Check your answers (the review page): Part 6 of repo:frontend read the live-animals set's one review page in full: the check-answers feature folder at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/ — page.js (id/slug/maturity), controller.js (the GET handler, the error summary assembly, the error precedence and which states hide answer errors), template.njk (the whole rendered page: view header, import reference numbers, section loop, summary-card loop, species blocks, groups and the foot form), refusal.js (the Continue refusal rules, unlisted-species errors and document-scan errors), review-href.js (the review URL's staleAction and refused flags), reviewed.js (recording the reviewed concurrency token), copy/copy.en.js and copy/copy.cy.js in full, every file under view-model/ (index.js, view-header.js, species-errors.js, invalid-parties.js, applicability.js, incomplete-cards.js; sections/about-consignment.js, description-of-goods.js, transport-and-arrival.js, documents.js, addresses.js, contact-address.js; cards/documents.js, cards/consignment/origin-of-import.js, what-are-you-importing.js, main-import-reason.js, additional-details.js, commodity-cards.js, cards/consignment/species/species-block.js, identification-details-table.js, identifier-columns.js, cards/movement/arrival-details.js, transport-details.js, cards/addresses/consignment-addresses.js, contact-address.js; rows/change-link.js, summary-row.js, value-text.js, party-row.js) and all 1,685 lines of check-answers.fit.spec.js. It covers the review page's route and maturity, its heading and title in every notification state, the view header (status tag, date line, Amend/Copy as new/Delete, import reference numbers), the six numbered sections and their anchors, every card and every row with its key, value formatting, change-link target and link text, the incomplete-card treatment and all ten Complete messages, the species and party error restatements, the invalid-party case, the Continue refusal rules and the states that hold errors silently, every behaviour the fit spec proves, and key parity between copy.cy.js and copy.en.js. The question pages that capture these answers, the shared layout, error-summary partial and journey strip, the commodities/addresses/documents/transport feature folders, the task rows and the obligations are other parts' and are only cited here where the review page's own files reach into them.
Part 7, Declaration, confirmation, delete and cancel amendment: Part 7, "Declaration, confirmation, delete and cancel amendment": the four feature folders that end a live-animals notification, read in full from repos/trade-imports-animals-frontend on main — src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/{declaration,confirmation,delete-notification,cancel-amend}. Each folder holds page.js (id, slug, maturity), controller.js (Hapi routes and handlers), template.njk (Nunjucks, extending shared/layout.njk), copy/copy.en.js and copy/copy.cy.js, and a co-located Playwright fit spec; declaration also has test-support.js and confirmation also has outstanding.js. Four pages are covered. (1) Declaration, /notifications/{journeyId}/declaration (GET and POST, slug 'declaration', maturity 'detailing'): a statements-and-one-checkbox page rendered only by POSTing step=review from the review page — its GET always redirects — with one required confirmation checkbox, a date-of-declaration line, a Continue button, and seven refusal paths (already-submitted, opened-before-review, unknown-step, changed-since-review, review-not-recorded, review-refused, not-ready-to-submit) that all redirect to the confirmation or the review. (2) Confirmation, /notifications/{journeyId}/confirmation (GET only, maturity 'detailing'): a govukPanel carrying the reference number, a conditional outstanding-items section computed by outstanding.js, then three fixed sections — Transporting the consignment, How to view or amend this notification (dashboard link plus a POST button that starts a new notification), and Getting help (APHA email, telephone, APHA Service Desk email, opening hours, HMRC and call-charges links) — and no back link. (3) Delete, /notifications/{journeyId}/delete (GET and POST, slug 'delete', maturity 'detailing'): a question-as-H1 confirmation page with a warning Yes button and a secondary No button back to the dashboard, allowed only for a draft, submitted or amending notification, redirecting to the dashboard with ?deleted=1 on success. (4) Cancel amendment, /notifications/{journeyId}/cancel-amend (GET and POST, slug from the shared kit, maturity 'detailing'): the same two-button shape, allowed only while the notification is amending, restoring the submitted snapshot and returning to the notification view with ?cancelled=1. The part also covers every behaviour the four fit specs prove (declaration 398 lines, confirmation 190, delete-notification 105, cancel-amend 192), including the axe checks and the no-JavaScript cancel-amendment path, and key parity between each copy.cy.js and its English twin. Routes are read against src/server/app/shared/paths.js (pageRoutePath = /notifications/{journeyId}/<slug>) and the slug constants in src/server/app/shared/kit.js (CYA_SLUG = 'notification-view', CANCEL_AMEND_SLUG = 'cancel-amend'); the engine helpers softDeleteJourney and cancelAmendJourney in src/server/app/engine/journey.js are cited only where a controller's observable outcome depends on them. The part stops at the review page (part 6) and the notification list (part 4): copy owned by shared/, check-answers or dashboard is cited but not claimed.
Part 8, Origin, main import reason and additional details: Part 8 read, in full, every file under the three non-commodity question folders of the about-the-consignment and description-of-the-goods sections of repos/trade-imports-animals-frontend's live-animals set, except the co-located *.test.js unit tests (controller.test.js, validate.test.js, copy/copy.test.js), which the scope leaves out. (1) journeys/linear/features/origin/: page.js (id/slug 'origin', maturity 'agreed'), evaluation.js (five obligation bindings), controller.js (120 lines: meta.collects, country item loading, per-country region-code prefix map, render, GET, POST, routes), template.njk (79 lines: accessible-autocomplete country field, Yes/No region-requirement radios with a conditional region-code input carrying a prefix, an optional internal-reference input, save actions with the return controls switched off), validate.js (163 lines: field order, trimming, prefix derivation, suffix normalisation, joined region code, country/region/internal-reference rules, blanks-on-change, fromAnswers/toAnswers), copy/copy.en.js and copy/copy.cy.js (title, country, region requirement, region code, internal reference and six error strings), and origin.fit.spec.js (856 lines, six describe blocks: the feature, region code and internal reference, the country type-ahead, the no-JavaScript path, country and region validation, internal-reference validation). (2) journeys/linear/features/import-reason/: page.js ('import-reason', 'agreed'), evaluation.js (five obligation bindings), controller.js (127 lines: reason and purpose option lists with per-value hints, country and port item lists, the exit-date field, render/GET/POST/routes), template.njk (85 lines: one radio set of reasons, each with its own reveal built from a shared autocomplete macro, plus an MOJ date picker), validate.js (153 lines: the REVEALS table, per-field country/port/purpose/date rules applied only to the chosen reason's reveals, payload and answer mapping, blanking of stale shared answers), copy/copy.en.js and copy/copy.cy.js (title, hidden legend, five reason hints, purpose legend and eleven purpose hints, country, port, date and seven error strings), and import-reason.fit.spec.js (853 lines, eight describe blocks: the feature, the reveals, reveal validation, the exit-date calendar position, destination territories, port and country type-ahead, temporary-admission port type-ahead, the no-JavaScript path and reveal accessibility). (3) journeys/linear/features/additional-details/: page.js ('additional-details', 'agreed'), evaluation.js (two obligation bindings), controller.js (105 lines: certification options from a service, Yes/No unweaned options, the in-scope test for the unweaned question, render/GET/POST/routes), template.njk (46 lines: two radio sets, the second shown only when the unweaned answer is in scope), validate.js (39 lines: oneOf rules for both radios, the unweaned applicability test shared with check-answers), copy/copy.en.js and copy/copy.cy.js (title, certification legend and hint, unweaned legend, hint and options, one error string), and additional-details.fit.spec.js (311 lines, four describe blocks: rendering, the unweaned commodity gate, validation, persistence and accessibility). It covers three routes (origin, import-reason, additional-details), their headings, captions, every field with its label, hint, options and whether it is required, every validation message in the three English copy files verbatim, every conditional reveal and what it asks, where Continue and Save and return lead, the save and failure behaviour, Welsh key parity for all three copy.cy.js files, and every behaviour the three fit specs prove. The reason, purpose and certification option labels are rendered from services outside this slice (services/import-reason-purpose, services/certification-purposes), and the country, subdivision and port lists from services/countries and services/ports, so those labels are recorded as gaps rather than invented.
Part 9, Commodity search and selection: Part 9, commodity search and selection, read the whole of src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/search/ except its *.test.js unit tests (search.controller.js, search.njk, _results.njk, search-results.njk, search-query.js, test-support.js, actions/commit-selection.js, selection/keys.js, selection/line-key.js, selection/remove-action.js, selection/rows.js, selection/selected-keys.js, view-model/commodity-groups.js, view-model/labels.js, view-model/result-order.js, view-model/selected-summary.js), plus the feature-level files the part names: page.js, evaluation.js, commodity-question-detour.js, lines.js, species-label.js, commodity-label.js, action-prefix.js, view-model/selected-commodity-rows.js, view-model/commodity-groups.js, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js, test-support.js, and the whole fit spec fit/search.fit.spec.js (847 lines, 8 describes, 31 tests). The slice is one page, the commodity search page at journey slug `commodities`, plus a second route it posts its result list to, `commodities/results`. Its layout is: a GET handler that renders search.njk (section caption, H1, inset, the shared appMultiSelectSearch macro wrapping the _results.njk macro, a help details block and the shared save actions); a POST handler on the page that branches four ways (search, clear, remove:<key>, or save); a POST handler on commodities/results that re-renders only the results macro inside search-results.njk with a screen-reader announcement; a selection/ layer that reads keys out of the payload, holds the result rows in flow-only answers under commoditySearchRows and orders keys canonically; a view-model/ layer that builds the grouped checkbox list, the bolded match labels and the chosen-species summary; and actions/commit-selection.js, which reconciles the commodityLines collection and redirects. The part covered that page's route and both handlers, its caption, H1, inset and help details, the search field with its label and hint, the Search, Add selection, Clear all and per-chip Remove controls, the result grouping, ordering, labelling, pre-ticking, match emphasis and no-results wording, the running selection summary, the one validation rule (Select a commodity), what a committed selection writes to commodityLines and where it leads, the commodity-question detour's return marker, the JavaScript enhancements and the no-JavaScript fallbacks the fit spec proves, the result list's measured styling, the English and Welsh copy keys the search page uses, and the mechanisms that build the selected-commodity rows and groups for the pages downstream. It leaves the commodity detail pages (consignment-details/, animal-identification/) and their copy keys to part 10.
Part 10, Commodity lines and animal identification: Part 10, Commodity lines and animal identification, read the two detail pages of the live-animals commodities feature in trade-imports-animals-frontend and everything they are built from, leaving the search and selection pages to part 9. Read in full: features/commodities/consignment-details/ (consignment-details.controller.js, fields.js, consignment-details.njk, _selected-commodities-table.njk, _species-quantities.njk, view-model/groups.js, view-model/selected-rows.js, view-model/values.js, validation/count-drop.js, remove/actions.js, remove/post-remove.js — skipping the three *.test.js unit tests); features/commodities/animal-identification/ (animal-identification.controller.js, animal-identification.njk, _identification-card.njk, _saved-animals-table.njk, _selected-commodities-summary.njk, animal-label.js, fields.js, line-cap.js, units-for-commodity-line.js, identified-animals.js, card/view-model.js, card/error-summary.js, identifier/fields.js, identifier/table.js, form/forms.js, records/append.js, remove/post-remove.js, summary/selected-commodities.js — skipping its two *.test.js files); the feature-level page.js, lines.js, species-label.js, commodity-label.js, action-prefix.js and copy/thousands-separators.js; copy/copy.en.js and copy/copy.cy.js; and the two fit specs fit/consignment-details.fit.spec.js (547 lines, 6 describes, 24 tests) and fit/identification.fit.spec.js (1,460 lines, 9 describes, 42 tests including a 10-case identifier-length loop and a no-JavaScript describe). Read for context but left to part 9: features/commodities/view-model/selected-commodity-rows.js and commodity-groups.js (which build both pages' tables), commodity-question-detour.js, and check-answers/view-model/applicability.js (packagesApply). An obligation id may not contain a path metacharacter ('.', '[' or ']'), and boot refuses one that does.

claims.statement: A row with nothing in scope reads not applicable; a row with no mandatory part reads optional while untouched, then fulfilled or in progress; and a row with mandatory parts reads fulfilled when each is satisfied, in progress when something is started, and not started otherwise.
An empty collection that is required still blocks a row from reading fulfilled, and an empty collection that is optional reads optional while a partly filled optional one reads in progress.

so the presentation-facing edge cases (empty optional collection -> OPTIONAL,

 * `requires.minEntries` or `requires.anyOfIds`) and stays a presentation
 * rule — the model emits nothing for a group with zero records, but an

claims.statement: The place of origin is always asked and always mandatory, and is stored as one composite address record.
The consignor is always asked and always mandatory.
The consignee is always asked and always mandatory.
The importer is always asked and always mandatory.
The place of destination is always asked and always mandatory.
The reason for import is always asked and always mandatory.
The purpose in the internal market is asked, and mandatory, only when the reason for import is internalMarket, and any stored purpose is dropped when the reason changes.
The destination country is asked, and mandatory, only when the reason for import is transit or transhipmentOrOnwardTravel, and is otherwise out of scope and purged.
claims.note: An existing ruling: the code records the V4 data dictionary (Confluence page 6497338582) as the authority for this rule.

claims.statement: The port of exit is asked, and mandatory, only when the reason for import is transit or temporaryAdmissionHorses, and is chosen from the same port list as the port of entry.
The exit date is asked, and mandatory, only when the reason for import is temporaryAdmissionHorses, and is otherwise out of scope and purged.
The contact address is always asked and always mandatory.
The internal reference number is trader-entered, always in scope and always optional.
What the animals are certified for is asked once for the whole notification and is always mandatory, although the spec notes APHA may make it depend on the commodity later.
The notification's approved reference number is assigned by the system when the notification is created and is never entered by a trader; it is mandatory but no page asks for it.
The notification's reference number is shaped GBN-AG-YY-XXXXXX, where the six-character body uses Crockford base32 (0-9 and A-Z without I, L, O or U).
A notification must hold at least one commodity line, and an empty list is refused under the code obligation.commodityLine.atLeastOne.
claims.note: The commodity lines group states no upper limit on the number of lines.

claims.statement: Every commodity line must carry a commodity code.
Every commodity line must carry a species Latin name.
A commodity line's species common name is optional.
Every commodity line must carry a number of animals.
A line's number of packages is asked only when that line's commodity code is in the package-count list, and even then it is optional.
The county parish holding number is asked, and mandatory, when any commodity line's code is in the CPH-required list, and is out of scope otherwise.
Whether the consignment contains unweaned animals is asked once for the whole notification, and only when any commodity line's code is in the unweaned list.

Each animal identifier record inside a commodity line must carry at least one of seven identifiers: a microchip, a passport, a tattoo, an ear tag, a horse name, identification details or a description; an empty record is refused under obligation.unitRecord.identifiersRequired.

The at-least-one-identifier floor is stood down unless more than one commodity line has a code in the identified list, so a consignment with a single identified line is not held to it at the collection level.
claims.quote:
floorAppliesToParent: moreThanOne(
      allowListed(commodityCode, identifiedCommodityCodes, null)
    )
---
 * The inner gate names the entries that would be asked; this wrapper stands
 * the whole rule down unless there are at least two of them, and otherwise
 * hands back the inner decision untouched with the same `fulfilmentIndexes`.
claims.note: mechanism: works on the commodity-lines collection. moreThanOne returns the inner allowListed decision only when it admits more than one entry, and otherwise reports out of scope.

claims.statement: A microchip is asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is in the microchip list, and is optional there.
A passport is asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is in the passport list, and is optional there.
A tattoo is asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is in the tattoo list, and is optional there.
An ear tag is asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is in the ear-tag list, and is optional there.
A horse name is asked of an animal only when its line's commodity code and species Latin name together are in the horse-name list, and is optional there.
claims.quote:
export const horseName = {
  id: HORSE_NAME_ID,
  name: 'horseName',
  within: unitRecord,
  status: 'optional',
  applyTo: allowListedPairs(
    commodityCode,
    speciesLatinName,
    horseNameCodeSpecies,
    unitRecord,
    [horseNameReason]
  )
}

claims.statement: Identification details are asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is outside the identified list, and are optional there.
A free-text description is asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is outside the identified list, and is optional there.
A permanent address is asked of an animal, and is mandatory, when its line's commodity code and species pair is in the permanent-address list.
claims.quote:
const permanentAddressPairGate = (reasons) =>
  allowListedPairs(
    commodityCode,
    speciesLatinName,
    permanentAddressCodeSpecies,
    unitRecord,

  name: 'permanentAddress',
  within: unitRecord,

claims.statement: Where that permanent address came from is asked on the same animals as the permanent address itself, and is optional.

claims.statement: A trader can attach between zero and fifteen accompanying documents to a notification, and a sixteenth is refused under obligation.accompanyingDocument.tooMany.
The fifteen-document cap is enforced on the stored notification as well as on the page's Add affordance, so a saved notification holding more than the cap is still caught afterwards.
Each accompanying document must carry its own type, attachment type, reference and date of issue; all four are mandatory within a document.
A document's upload id and filename are optional, so a document can be recorded without a file attached.
The V4 data dictionary page still reads as if a notification can hold at most one accompanying document, and the obligation model is treated as the authority until that page is amended.
claims.note: An existing ruling recorded in code: a known disagreement with the V4 source, resolved in favour of the model.

claims.statement: Each document's instance id is a session-scoped counter value such as doc1 or doc2.
claims.quote: // Instance ids are session-scoped counter values (`doc1`, `doc2`, …).

claims.statement: A gate that reads one stored answer and swaps the mandate keeps the answer in scope on both branches, while one that swaps in scope drops the stored answer when the gate answer flips.
claims.quote:
Both
 * `whenTrue` and `whenFalse` are returned verbatim, so a caller who
 * passes two in-scope decisions gets a pure status flip (e.g.
 * `regionCode` mandatory ↔ optional), and one in-scope + one
 * out-of-scope gets a purge-on-flip (e.g. `purposeInInternalMarket`
 * dropped when `reasonForImport` changes).

claims.statement: A per-line or per-animal gate decides entry by entry, so one commodity line can be asked for an identifier while another in the same consignment is not.
claims.quote:
/**
 * allowListed — in scope on entries where `gateObligation`'s stored
 * value is in the allowlist.
 *
 * - Depth-1 (gate + gated at the same identity level): pass `null` for
 *   `gatedParentGroup`; fulfilmentIndexes are the passing gate keys.
 * - Depth-N > 1 (gate broader than gated): pass the gated obligation's
 *   parent group as `gatedParentGroup`; fulfilmentIndexes are that
 *   group's fulfilmentIndexes whose ancestor prefix has a passing gate.

claims.statement: An answer that is blank never counts as outside an allowlist, so a commodity line with no code yet is not treated as an unidentified species.
claims.quote:
/**
 * notInUnionOf — dual of `allowListed`. In scope on entries whose
 * `gateObligation` stored value is not blank and not in the union of the
 * given allowlists. The union is derived at call-time and exposed on
 * `.metadata.values`.

claims.statement: The commodity search asks the reference data service for GET /commodities with the search term as q and the page and size as query parameters.
The species check asks the reference data service for POST /commodities/species-check with the commodity lines in the body.

claims.statement: The species check returns the commodity lines whose Latin name is not listed under their commodity code, and an empty list when every line's species is listed.
claims.quote:
/**
 * @param {Array<{code: string, latinName: string}>} lines - the lines to check.

claims.statement: No species check is made at all when there are no commodity lines to check.
A species-check reply that carries no unlisted list is treated as a failure rather than as 'nothing unlisted'.

When the service is run in stub mode both the commodity search and the species check are answered from the service's own fixtures instead of reference data, and stub mode is never honoured in production.
A reference data failure is turned into a 503 'Reference data unavailable' naming the dataset that failed, either 'commodities' or 'species'.
Every call to reference data carries the service's trace headers and a JSON content type, and any non-OK reply is raised as a failure carrying the status, status text and URL.

Six commodity codes carry per-animal identifiers: cattle 0102 (ear tag, passport, tattoo), horses 0101 (microchip, passport and a horse name for Equus cabalus), swine 0103 (ear tag, tattoo), sheep 010410 (ear tag), goats 010420 (ear tag) and other live mammals 01061900 (microchip, passport, tattoo).
Those same six codes are the identified list, so a commodity line with any other code is treated as unidentified and asked for identification details and a description instead.
claims.quote: export const IDENTIFIED_CODES = Object.keys(COMMODITY_IDENTIFIERS)

Horses (0101) ask for a package count but do not require a CPH number; the three 0407 egg codes require a CPH number but ask for no package count.

claims.statement: Four commodity codes carry a description: 0101 'Live horses, asses, mules and hinnies', 0102 'Live bovine animals', 01061900 'Other live animals' and 0301 'Live fish'.
Three commodity codes carry a short name: 0101 'Horse', 0102 'Cattle' and 0301 'Fish'.
Live fish, commodity code 0301, has a description and a short name but no identifiers, so a fish consignment is asked for identification details and a description rather than a tag or passport.
claims.quote: export const LIVE_FISH_CODE = '0301'
claims.note: 0301 is absent from COMMODITY_IDENTIFIERS, so it is outside IDENTIFIED_CODES and the notInUnionOf gates for identification details and description admit it.

claims.statement: The per-identifier code lists are derived from the one identifier table rather than written out, so a code that carries an identifier is always in that identifier's list.
claims.note: mechanism: turns the identifier table into per-identifier code lists, and into code-and-species pairs for an identifier that names a species.

claims.statement: A commodity search in stub mode matches a group when the term is a prefix of its CN code, and otherwise matches a species when every word of the term is a prefix of consecutive words of its Latin or common name.
claims.note: mechanism: the stub's own matching over the captured commodity fixtures; an empty term matches nothing by name, and a code prefix match returns the group's whole species list.

claims.statement: Stub search results are paged by slicing the flattened matches and then regrouping them by code, so a group can be split across two pages and the total counts species rather than groups.
claims.note: mechanism: paging over the stub's flattened code-and-species matches.

claims.statement: In stub mode a commodity line counts as unlisted when the captured fixtures hold no group with that code carrying that exact Latin name.
claims.quote:
const listedInStub = ({ code, latinName }) =>
  COMMODITY_GROUPS.some(
    (group) =>
      group.code === code &&
      group.species.some((species) => species.latinName === latinName)
  )

export const unlistedLinesInStub = (lines) =>
  lines.filter((line) => !listedInStub(line))

claims.statement: Four answers decide which conditional questions a trader sees, and they are exercised as a cross product of 48 states: whether a region code is required, the reason for import (unanswered, internal market, transit or temporary admission of horses), the means of transport (unanswered or road vehicle) and the transporter type (unanswered, commercial or private).
claims.quote:
/**
 * The scope-determining flags whose cross-product spans the conditional
 * obligations moving into and out of scope: the region-code requirement, the
 * import reason, the means of transport and the transporter type. The reason
 * axis carries transit and temporary-admission values so the reason-gated
 * destinationCountry / portOfExit / exitDate obligations are exercised.
 * 2×4×2×3 = 48 states.
 *
 * @returns {Array<object>} 48 partial answer states.
 */

claims.statement: The journey's reachability is proved over 240 answer states, each of the five seed variants overlaid with each of the 48 scope states, with unanswered values left out rather than stored blank.
claims.note: 5 seed variants × 48 scope states = 240 answer states.

claims.statement: Two answers are the required earlier answers every later page needs before it will open: the country of origin and at least one commodity line.
claims.note: Matches the two obligations named in ENFORCED_AT_CONTINUE, countryOfOrigin and commodityCode.

claims.statement: Only a single-valued answer can take part in the address-book hand-off: a party bound to a repeating answer is refused outright with 'Party fulfilment mapping only supports scalar bindings'.
The INS address book returns the trader to /live-animals/notifications/{journeyId}/address-return, a page reached by GET only.
claims.note: It is registered with the addresses page's own route options, so it is reached under the same conditions as the page itself.

claims.statement: The return carries four things in its query: fulfilment-id, handshake-token, addressId and landing.
The landing the address book names may be one of three: select, return or cancel.
A return naming a fulfilment id the service does not know is refused with a 400 Bad Request reading 'Unknown fulfilment', and the refusal is logged as 'Address return refused'.
A return naming a landing that is not select, return or cancel is refused with a 400 Bad Request reading 'Unknown landing'.
A return that names a landing other than cancel but no address is refused with a 400 Bad Request reading 'Missing address'.
A return that names no landing at all but does carry an address is treated as a selection.
A return that names neither a landing nor an address — someone simply coming back — takes the trader to that party's address picker, saves nothing and needs no handshake token.
claims.note: The token check comes after this branch, so a bare return is always honoured.

claims.statement: Every other return must carry the handshake token the service issued for that fulfilment id, and one that does not is refused with a 400 Bad Request reading 'Invalid handshake'.
claims.note: Security: this is the check that stops a return being replayed or forged for a party the trader never started a hand-off for. The token is compared against the trader's own cookie, so a return cannot be honoured in someone else's session.

claims.statement: A handshake token is used once: it is forgotten as soon as the return is accepted, and the whole cookie is dropped once no hand-off is outstanding.
A trader who cancels in the address book is returned to the notification overview, and nothing is saved.

An address returned as a selection is read back from the address book, copied onto the party as its answer, and the trader is taken to that party's return page — the Consignment addresses page for all five consignment parties — with the added-address banner naming it.
An address returned with the 'return' landing is read back and the banner is shown, but it is not saved onto the party: the trader is taken to that party's address picker to choose it there.
claims.note: So 'select' means the address book chose the party's address for the trader, and 'return' means it only added the address to the book.

claims.statement: The returned address is read scoped to the organisation on the trader's signed-in session, so a record belonging to another organisation is never returned.
claims.note: Security: the address id comes from the query, so the organisation scope on the read is what keeps the lookup to the trader's own address book.

claims.statement: An address that has been deleted, or that is not offered for the party's address-book role, is treated as though it had never been chosen.

When the returned address cannot be found in the trader's address book, nothing is saved and the party's address picker is shown again with the message 'The address could not be found in your address book. Select another address or try adding it again.'

When the address book cannot be reached while reading the returned address, nothing is saved and the party's address picker is shown again with the message 'The address book could not be reached. Your answers on this page have been saved. Try again in a few minutes.'
claims.note: An error that is not a recoverable backend error is not swallowed: it is raised and handled as a server error.

claims.statement: When the selected address was read but could not be saved onto the party, the trader is sent to that party's address picker with the same address-book-unavailable message, rather than being left thinking the address was saved.
Every honoured return is logged as 'Returned from the address book' with the notification, the party, the landing and the address id.
The handshake error is passed to the party's picker page as a query parameter, and an empty value is left off the URL altogether.
claims.note: mechanism: builds the redirect URL back to a party page, dropping empty query values.

claims.statement: A return from the address book does not carry the trader's trail, so the Back link on the Consignment addresses page they land on falls back to the notification overview.
claims.quote: return h.redirect(pagePath(journeyId, party.returnSlug))
claims.note: Follows because every redirect in the return handler builds a plain page path with no trail, and trailBackLink falls back to the overview when a request carries no trail.

claims.statement: The address book's own return URL is not recorded in this repo: nothing in the addresses feature says how the INS address book is told where to come back to.
claims.note: Looked at the four query parameters the add-address hand-off sends, the url helper it uses, and the whole return handler. The helpers that build view-an-address URLs take an explicit `return` path, but the add-address hand-off sends no return path — the address book must derive the address-return URL from journey-type and notification-id itself.

   `shared` and `analysis` directories under `src/server/app/`: set-agnostic
   platform code
3. L3 — `sets/<set>/obligations/`: one set's obligation data
4. L4 — `sets/<set>/journeys/<style>/`: one journey's pages and topology

is only the export barrel. Each set
has a gateway of its own beside it — today

it maps a page id to the name of
the section of the journey that page belongs to, which `kit.base()` puts in the

claims.statement: The platform records that prerequisites are strictly-earlier fields enforced when the user continues, and that the page which asks for the first of a page's missing required earlier answers is the earliest in page order.
claims.quote:

strictly-earlier fields that are enforced when the user continues. It reads the
configured section list through the journey-flow seam. It also answers which page
asks for the first of a page's missing required earlier answers: the earliest in page
order.

claims.statement: The platform records that the journey's page order is the set's flow sections read in order, and that a step is a page belonging to a task row and not marked as a sub-page, while a sub-page keeps its section's status and prerequisites but is reached only from the page that opens it.

owns the journey's
page order and the next page after one. The order is the set's flow sections
read in order. A step is a page that belongs to a task row and is not marked as
a sub-page; a sub-page keeps its section's status and prerequisites but is

claims.statement: The platform records that Save and continue lands on the next step that applies when the page gate also passes, else on the page asking for the first missing required earlier answer, that it answers nothing past the last step and throws for a page in no section, and that kit.nextTarget logs once when the landing is the asking page and falls back to the review page when it answers nothing.

`nextStepLanding()` answers where Save
and continue lands after a page: the next step that applies (`pageAppliesTo()` in
[`gates.js`](../flow/gates.js): the page's own gate, else some obligation it
collects in scope) when `pageGatePasses()` also holds for it, else the page that asks
for the first missing required earlier answer, with the unopened page and the
missing answer ids. It answers nothing past the last step, and throws for a page in no
section. `kit.nextTarget` uses it after the explicit exits, logs once when the landing
is the asking page, and falls back to the review page when it answers nothing.

claims.statement: The platform records that a valid Save and continue goes to the next page in the journey's one page order that applies, and from the last page that applies to check your answers, however the page was reached, including a new notification, a copy, the Overview, a reopened draft, a new browser session, a check your answers Change link or an amendment.

A valid Save and continue therefore goes to the next page in the journey's one page
order that applies, and from the last page that applies to check your answers,
however the page was reached: a new notification, a copy, the Overview, a reopened
draft, a new browser session, a check your answers Change link or an amendment.

`subPage: true` is reached only from the page that opens it and keeps its section's
status and prerequisites. A page in no section is a detour off a list page, such as the
transporter add pages. A page in no task row, such as the review, declaration and
confirmation, is not a step.

A

helpers.

claims.statement: The platform records that each gate helper returns an applyTo giving a decision and carrying metadata describing the gate, that an obligation may declare dependsOn naming the obligations its gate reads, and that a coverage assertion fails the build for a gated obligation without a complete declared or derived dependsOn.
claims.quote:

which gives a decision, and carries a `.metadata` property that describes the gate. An
obligation may also declare `dependsOn`, the ids of the obligations its gate reads.
The reachability prover inverts gates from this data, and a coverage assertion fails
the build for a gated obligation without a complete declared or derived `dependsOn`.

claims.statement: The platform records that a decision naming which fulfilment indexes are in scope uses allowListed or notInUnionOf, with null passed for gatedParentGroup when gate and gated obligation sit at the same level and the group passed when the gated obligation is deeper, the engine then fanning across that group's fulfilment indexes for each matching parent.
claims.quote:
- A decision naming which fulfilment indexes are in scope, typically when the
  obligation is indexed: `allowListed` or `notInUnionOf`. Pass `null` for
  `gatedParentGroup` when the gate and the gated obligation sit at the same level,
  or the group when the gated obligation is deeper; the engine then fans across
  that group's fulfilment indexes for each matching parent.

claims.statement: The platform records that allowListedPairs admits a fulfilment index whose two values form a listed pair, and that the permanent address is asked only of a line whose CN code and Latin name are listed together.

claims.statement: The platform records that moreThanOne is a combinator rather than a gate: it stands another helper down unless that helper admits more than one entry, and it goes on a group's requires, never on an obligation's applyTo.
claims.quote:
- `moreThanOne` is a combinator, not a gate: it stands another helper down unless
  that helper admits more than one entry. It goes on a group's `requires` (for
  example `floorAppliesToParent`), never on an obligation's `applyTo`.

claims.statement: The platform records that the reachability prover builds a witness for a complement gate from a stable sentinel string outside the gate's derived union, and reports the gate opaque rather than vacuously green if the union held the sentinel and its fallback, because a gate no input can open is an authoring defect.
claims.quote:
The reachability prover builds a witness for a complement gate (`notInUnionOf`,
`anyNotInUnionOf`) from a stable sentinel string that is not in the gate's derived
union. If the union held the sentinel and its fallback as well, the prover reports
the gate opaque instead of vacuously green, because a gate no input can open is an
authoring defect. A commodity-code union covers a handful of codes, so any other
string opens the gate.

builds an index for the configured manifest, evaluates applicability, converges
scope and purges fulfilments that are unknown or out of scope. Evaluation is pure:
answers and fulfilments go in; derived views and cleaned fulfilment come out.

claims.statement: The set records that collections use hand-written controllers over generic engine operations: documents keeps its entry form and read-back list on one page, the commodity search reconciles selected lines before the details page edits them and its results route renders only the results for the page's multi-select search to swap in, and animal identification manages a nested collection within one commodity line.
claims.quote: Collections use hand-written controllers over generic engine operations.

claims.statement: The set records that the engine supplies collection facts and mutation primitives while the feature owns rows, links, copy and validation.
claims.quote:
The engine supplies collection facts and mutation primitives. The feature owns rows,
links, copy and validation.

claims.statement: The set records that controller and copy tests sit beside the feature, browser specs use *.fit.spec.js and run in the Playwright features project, and feature tests include initial and error-state accessibility checks.
claims.quote:
Controller and copy tests sit beside the feature. Browser specs use
`*.fit.spec.js` and run in the Playwright `features` project. Feature tests include
initial and error-state accessibility checks.

claims.statement: The set records that its obligation manifest imports the declarations in obligations/sections/, exports each obligation, builds the ordered obligations array and derives groups from within references.
claims.quote:
It imports the declarations in `obligations/sections/`, exports each obligation,
builds the ordered `obligations` array and derives `groups` from `within`
references.

claims.statement: The set records that its declarations are divided by domain into nine sections: arrival, commodities including aggregates, identifiers and line fields, documents, import reason, miscellaneous consignment details, origin, parties, system values and transport.
claims.quote:
- arrival
- commodities, including aggregates, identifiers and line fields
- documents
- import reason
- miscellaneous consignment details
- origin
- parties
- system values
- transport

claims.statement: The set records that its declarations contain stable identity, scope, mandate and cardinality rules but no display copy or journey knowledge.
claims.quote:
They contain stable
identity, scope, mandate and cardinality rules, but no display copy or journey
knowledge.

claims.statement: The set records the ruling that the CPH question is asked when any commodity line's code is on the CPH-required list, and that a line with no code yet is ignored rather than counted as a match.
claims.quote:
The CPH question is asked when any commodity line's code is on the CPH-required
list; a line with no code yet is ignored rather than counted as a match
(`anyAllowListed`).

claims.statement: The set records that the animal identifiers floor asks for a record per commodity line only on a consignment carrying more than one identified commodity line.
claims.quote:
The animal identifiers floor asks for a record per commodity
line only on a consignment carrying more than one identified commodity line
(`moreThanOne` over the identified-commodity allowlist).

claims.statement: The set records that the journey's feature bindings import the same obligation objects as the manifest, the shared object identity letting the fulfilment registry check that every leaf is owned once and that grouped binding paths match each within chain.
claims.quote:
The journey's feature bindings import the same obligation objects from this set.
This shared object identity lets the fulfilment registry check that every leaf is
owned once and that grouped binding paths match each `within` chain.

claims.statement: The set records that its allow-list test checks the commodity allow-lists against the set-owned reference service, each list's describe iterating its own allow-list and checking that a control value on no list leaves the obligation out of scope.
claims.quote:
checks the commodity allow-lists against the set-owned reference service; each
list's describe iterates its own allow-list and checks that a control value on
no list leaves the obligation out of scope

claims.statement: The set records that the package-count check instead iterates every code the captured catalogue serves and asserts the exact served codes the list leaves out, so a code new to the capture fails there, that one anti-drift describe pins every list's exact contents against an expected map, and that changing an allow-list on purpose means editing rules.js and updating the matching expected list in the same change.
claims.quote:
the package-count describe
instead iterates every code the set's captured catalogue serves and asserts
the exact served codes the list leaves out, which is where a code new to the
capture fails; one anti-drift describe pins every list's exact contents
against the expected map, so a single-file edit to a service list fails
there; to change an allow-list on purpose, edit it in
[`rules.js`](../services/commodities/rules.js) and update the matching expected list
in the test in the same change.

claims.statement: The set records that accompanying documents are capped at fifteen entries, the set manifest declaring the cardinality and the documents feature enforcing it on its write path.
claims.quote:
The document collection has a maximum of fifteen entries. The set manifest declares
the cardinality and the documents feature enforces it on its write path.
claims.note: Verified against the code: obligations/sections/documents.js:25 holds `maxEntries: 15` with error code `obligation.accompanyingDocument.tooMany`.

claims.statement: The set records that species come from MDM through reference-data and that the commodity rules — the identifier, package-count, permanent-address, unweaned, CPH-required and type rules — are set data that must match MDM's spelling exactly.
claims.quote:
Species come from MDM through reference-data. The rules in
[`rules.js`](../services/commodities/rules.js) are set data: the identifier,
package-count, permanent-address, unweaned, CPH-required and type rules. They must
match MDM's spelling exactly.

claims.statement: The set records that canonical fulfilment can hold values one backend projection cannot represent, that Mapper B layers its additional fields over Mapper A, and that a new obligation always needs a feature binding but only gets a mapper field when the target backend schema has a real home for it.
claims.quote:
Canonical fulfilment can contain values that one backend projection cannot
represent. Mapper B layers its additional fields over Mapper A. A new obligation
always needs a feature binding, but it only gets a mapper field when the target
backend schema has a real home for it.

claims.statement: The set records that Commodity details refuses a number of animals, and a number of packages, above 2,147,483,647 on each species line, because the animals backend holds those counts in Java Integer fields.
claims.ref: src/server/app/sets/live-animals/docs/limits.md:24 (A number of animals or packages above what the backend's field can hold is refused)
claims.quote:
Commodity details refuses a number of animals, and a number of packages,
above 2,147,483,647 on each species line. The animals backend's
`CommodityComplement.totalNoOfAnimals`, `CommodityComplement.totalNoOfPackages`
and `Species.noOfPackages` are Java `Integer` fields, so a count above their
range is rejected by the backend rather than stored.

claims.statement: The set records that the cap guards each line's own number and not the totals the backend derives from it, so several lines under one CN code can still sum past the field's range and nothing in the frontend refuses that.
claims.quote:
The cap guards each line's own number, not the totals the backend derives
from it.
claims.note: The ledger records this as a known, unrefused edge: "several lines under one CN code can still sum past the field's range, and nothing in the frontend refuses that".

claims.statement: The set records that grouped fulfilment tokens such as line0 and unit1 are positions in one canonical snapshot rather than durable record identifiers, so removing an earlier entry can renumber later entries.
claims.quote:
Grouped fulfilment tokens such as `line0` and `unit1` are positions in one canonical
snapshot, not durable record identifiers. Removing an earlier entry can renumber
later entries.

The dashboard's Welsh copy is a machine draft that a translator has not

draft as well. A translator must review it in the same file, where it is a

claims.quote:

claims.quote:
The declaration's Welsh responsibility bullets both complete the "nes iddo naill

claims.statement: The set records that all thirteen Welsh document-type labels are machine drafts a translator must review, the upload page and the review page both reading them, and that the ones carrying a slash need the most attention because each joins two document names the English list pairs and Welsh mutation after the joiner has not been checked.

claims.statement: The set records that the permanent address page's Welsh copy and the consignment addresses page's permanent address section leaves are the same machine draft, neither to be shipped without Welsh Language Standards sign-off.
claims.quote:
The permanent address page's Welsh is a machine draft too. A translator must
review it in `journeys/linear/features/permanent-address/copy/copy.cy.js`.
The consignment addresses page's permanent address section leaves in
`journeys/linear/features/addresses/copy/copy.cy.js` are the same machine draft

claims.statement: The set's copy-status record names no page-maturity level: it records which copy is unreviewed Welsh and nothing about whether a page's copy is agreed, the four maturity levels being recorded in features.md instead.

The repo's only record of agreed copy is the page-maturity level on each page.js (features.md:16, claim repo-frontend-p19-065) and page-design.md's one remark that a particular button and its copy are "agreed for now" (claim on the Commodity pages heading). Nothing in the repo records English copy as content-reviewed.

claims.statement: The live-animals journey records eight ordered flow sections, a flow section being an Overview group, and the sections together being the journey's one page order, the order Overview lists its tasks in.
claims.quote:
exports eight ordered `sections`. A flow

order: the order Overview lists its tasks in.
