This journey's
required earlier answers are where the consignment is coming from and what is being
imported.

claims.statement: The journey records that the review section has the one authored section gate, requiring scope.readyForCheckYourAnswers, and that normal page gates are derived from meta.collects, scope and the required earlier answers.
claims.quote:
The `review` section has the one authored section
gate: it requires `scope.readyForCheckYourAnswers`. Normal page gates are derived
from `meta.collects`, scope and the required earlier answers.

claims.statement: The journey records that the consignment-parties section holds the CPH number page, then the permanent address page, then Consignment addresses, so each sub-page goes on to Consignment addresses and Consignment addresses goes on to the contact address.
claims.quote:
The `consignment-parties` section holds the CPH number page, then the permanent address page,
then Consignment addresses, so each sub-page, marked `subPage: true` on its page identity, goes on
to Consignment addresses and Consignment addresses goes on to the contact address.

claims.statement: The journey records that consignment-parties is a stable section id the journey spec and the prototype share, while its caption and group heading read "Addresses".
claims.quote: The section id `consignment-parties` is a stable id that the journey spec and the prototype share. Its caption and group heading read "Addresses".
claims.note: One of the few places the repo's ledger records the prototype itself as the reason for a name.

claims.statement: The journey records four flow-only keys kept in the session's flow-only store rather than canonical obligation fulfilment and never sent to the backend: declaration, commoditySearchRows, the values an add-transporter form is keeping after a refused save held per transporter type, and the name of the transporter a save has just added, read once by the transporter list for its success banner.
claims.quote:
`FLOW_ONLY_KEYS` contains `declaration` and `commoditySearchRows`, plus the two
keys the transport feature's own add-session module owns: the values an
add-transporter form is keeping after a refused save, held per transporter
type, and the name of the transporter a save has just added, read once by
the transporter list for its success banner. All four are kept in the
session's flow-only store rather than canonical obligation fulfilment, and
are never sent to the backend.

claims.statement: The journey records that the transport section lists one transporter step, the transporter list, and that the pages which add a transporter are detours off that list belonging to no section.
claims.quote:
The transport section lists one transporter step, the transporter list. The pages
that add a transporter are detours off that list and belong to no section.

claims.statement: The journey records twelve task rows, a task row grouping pages on Overview and being a submit-readiness unit rather than a flow section, deciding nothing about where Save and continue goes.
claims.quote:
exports twelve `taskRows`. A
task row groups pages on Overview and is a submit-readiness unit; it is not a flow
section, and it decides nothing about where Save and continue goes.

claims.statement: The journey records that most row status comes from the union of each page's collects, that parts narrows a row to a collection facet, and that the commodity line is split three ways — the selection on the commodities row, the numbers on the consignmentDetails row, the identifiers on the animalIdentification row — so each of the three pages over that one collection carries a status of its own.
claims.quote:
Most row status comes from the union of each page's `collects`. `parts` narrows a
row to a collection facet. The commodity line is split three ways — the selection
on the `commodities` row, the numbers on the `consignmentDetails` row, the
identifiers on the `animalIdentification` row — so each of the three pages over
that one collection carries a status of its own.

claims.statement: The journey records that the commodities row claims its facet with except rather than only, so a new member of the collection defaults to that row instead of falling out of all three, that conditional: true lets the hub hide a row that is not applicable, and that every row contributes to readyForCheckYourAnswers.
claims.quote:
The `commodities` row claims its
facet with `except` rather than `only`, so a new member of the collection defaults
to that row instead of falling out of all three. `conditional: true` lets the hub
hide a row that is not applicable. Every row contributes to
`readyForCheckYourAnswers`.

claims.statement: The journey records that applies is the escape hatch for a row whose parts cannot express its applicability, rowStatus reading Not applicable when it answers no whatever the parts would have rolled up to.
claims.quote:
`applies` is the escape hatch for a row whose parts cannot express its
applicability. `rowStatus` calls it with the answers and reads Not applicable when
it answers no, whatever the parts would have rolled up to.

claims.statement: The journey records that the animal identification row needs applies because its part, the commodityLines collection, is a structural group in scope from the moment the notification exists so the roll-up never reaches Not applicable, while the transit-countries row needs no applies because its answer leaves scope on its own.
claims.quote:
The animal
identification row needs it: its part is the `commodityLines` collection, a
structural group in scope from the moment the notification exists, so the roll-up
never reaches Not applicable and `conditional: true` on its own would leave the row
drawn. Reach for `applies` only when a scope condition genuinely cannot carry the
rule — the transit-countries row needs no `applies`, because its answer leaves
scope on its own.

claims.statement: The journey records that extraAnswerGiven is the second escape hatch, for a row owing an answer no part key can reach, because a leaf nested inside a collection such as the permanent address inside animalIdentifiers inside commodityLines has no part key of its own.
claims.quote:
`extraAnswerGiven` is the second escape hatch, for a row that owes an answer no
part key can reach. A scope key is a bare obligation name or a collection name, so
a leaf nested inside a collection — the permanent address inside `animalIdentifiers`
inside `commodityLines` — has no part key of its own.

claims.statement: The journey records that the addresses row declares extraAnswerGiven, a predicate over the answers and the evaluation, and that rowStatus holds that row at In progress rather than Completed while it answers false, whatever the parts roll up to.
claims.quote:
The addresses row declares
`extraAnswerGiven`, a predicate over the answers and the evaluation in the same
shape as `applies`, and `rowStatus` holds the row at In progress rather than
Completed while it answers false, whatever the parts roll up to.
claims.note: In progress is the internal row status; page-design.md records that the hub shows only Complete or To do on screen.

claims.statement: The journey records that the hub derives its groups from the flow sections, each section holding a task row's first page being a group headed by its caption and listing its task rows in the order of their first page, and that the session holds no record of how a notification was started.
claims.quote:
The hub derives its groups from the flow sections: each section that holds a task
row's first page is a group, headed by its caption, and lists its task rows in the
order of their first page. The sections are also the journey's page order, which
Save and continue follows from every start. The session holds no record of how a
notification was started.

claims.statement: The journey records the design-release decision that a trader may start any task on the notification in any order: no row on the hub is ever shut, every row is a link carrying a real status from the moment the notification exists, nothing on the page says "Cannot start yet", and a row that does not apply leaves the list instead.
claims.quote:
No row on the hub is ever shut: every row is a link carrying a real status from
the moment the notification exists, and nothing on the page says "Cannot start
yet". A row that does not apply to this consignment leaves the list instead
(`conditional`, and `applies` where the parts cannot express it).

claims.statement: The journey records that the review is not a task row at all: it is reached from a primary "Review and submit" button under the task list, beside the secondary "Return to dashboard", and is offered whatever the notification still owes, the review page rendering an unfinished notification and naming what is outstanding.
claims.quote:
The review is not a task row at all. Design release 1 reaches it from a primary
"Review and submit" button under the task list, beside the secondary "Return to
dashboard", and offers it whatever the notification still owes — the review page
renders an unfinished notification and names what is outstanding.

claims.statement: The journey records that the review section's authored gate on readyForCheckYourAnswers stands between the review page and submitting, the declaration refusing on the same verdict.
claims.quote:
The review
section's authored gate on `readyForCheckYourAnswers` still stands between that
page and submitting: the declaration refuses on the same verdict.

claims.statement: The journey records that the declaration is reachable only from the review: the review's Continue posts to /declaration with step=review, the review registers no POST of its own and GET /declaration redirects to the review, so the user has seen the review in its latest state before submitting.
claims.quote:
The declaration is reachable only from the review. The review's
Continue posts to `/declaration` with `step=review` - the review registers no
`POST` of its own, and `GET /declaration` redirects to the review. This is to
ensure that the user has seen the review in its latest state before submitting
the notification.

claims.statement: The journey records that the declaration page renders the concurrency token the review page rendered rather than the current one, and that the declaration submit works only while the current token still matches it, so a notification changed after the review rendered sends the trader back to the review with the "notification has been updated" banner.
claims.quote:
The declaration page renders the same concurrency
token as the review page (RT), rather than the current concurrency token. The
declaration submit (`step=declare`) only works if the current concurrency token
is still the same as RT, meaning that the notification is unchanged. If the
notification changed after the review rendered — another tab, another user — the
token no longer matches and the trader goes back to the review with the
"notification has been updated" banner (`?staleAction=1`).

claims.statement: The journey records that the review's GET records the concurrency token in the session and both declaration steps require the posted token to match it, so a token copied off another page cannot reach the declaration without the review.
claims.quote:
The review's GET also records the token in the session
(`check-answers/reviewed.js`), and both declaration steps require the posted
token to match it, so a token copied off another page cannot reach the
declaration without the review.
claims.note: Security-relevant: the ledger records this as the control that stops a declaration being reached without the review.

claims.statement: The journey records that a refused Continue or Submit goes back with ?refused=1, which moves focus to the review's error summary, and that the review names every refusal itself, still-scanning documents included.
claims.quote:
A refused Continue or Submit goes back with
`?refused=1`, which moves focus to the review's error summary; the review names
every refusal itself, still-scanning documents included.

claims.statement: The journey records that letting every row be startable puts the cost on the pages rather than the hub: a page behind a row has to render and save sensibly when nothing else has been answered, and where there is genuinely nothing to ask yet the page says so itself.
claims.quote:
That puts the cost on the pages, not the hub: a page behind a row has to render
and save sensibly when nothing else has been answered. Where there is genuinely
nothing to ask yet the page says so itself

claims.statement: The journey records that the consignment details page redirects to the commodity question when the notification holds no line, and that the transit countries page sends a load or any submit to the overview, saving nothing, when the means of transport leaves transit countries out of scope.

the consignment-details page
([`consignment-details.controller.js`](../journeys/linear/features/commodities/consignment-details/consignment-details.controller.js))
redirects to the commodity question when the notification holds no line, and
the transit countries page
([`transit-countries.controller.js`](../journeys/linear/features/transport/transit-countries/transit-countries.controller.js))
sends a load or any submit to the overview, saving nothing, when the means of
transport leaves transit countries out of scope.

claims.statement: The journey records that its entry guard owns the redirect policy before handlers run, along with the Import Notification Service's type question URL the gateway passes to configureJourneyFlow().
claims.quote:
owns the journey's redirect
policy before handlers run and the Import Notification Service's type question
(`insTypeQuestionUrl`), which the gateway passes to `configureJourneyFlow()`.

claims.statement: The journey records a table of where Back opens for each way the trader arrived: Save and continue on another page opens that page carrying the places beneath it; an Overview task row or review button opens Overview; a review Change link or error link opens the review; a dashboard card (View or Amend) opens the dashboard; starting a new notification opens the dashboard from the first page; arriving from the Import Notification Service opens its type question for this notification from the first page; and nothing the journey knows opens Overview.
claims.quote:
| Save and continue on another page     | That page, carrying the places beneath it            |
| An Overview task row or review button | Overview                                             |
| A review Change link or error link    | The review                                           |
| A dashboard card (View or Amend)      | The dashboard                                        |
| Start a new notification              | The dashboard, from the first page                   |
| The Import Notification Service       | Its type question for this notification, first page  |
| Nothing the journey knows             | Overview (the first page: see the entry guard below) |

claims.statement: The journey records that following a Back link ends nothing: a later Save and continue goes on to the next page that applies, adding the page saved to the trail, so Back steps through the visited pages in reverse, while Save and return to overview still goes to the overview.
claims.quote:
Following a Back link does not end anything: a later Save and continue goes on to the
next page that applies, adding the page saved to the trail, so Back steps through the
visited pages in reverse. Save and return to overview still goes to the overview.

claims.statement: The journey records that a round trip to a sub-page keeps where the trader came from, so the page that opened it still goes Back where it did before, the permanent address page, add transporter and a picker's View link each carrying the trail out and back.
claims.quote:
A round trip to a sub-page keeps where the trader came from, so the page that opened
it still goes Back where it did before: the permanent address page, add transporter
and a picker's View link each carry the trail out and back.

claims.statement: The journey records that the identification page's no-commodity-line guard carries the trail on to What are you importing? so Back there opens the page the trader came from, and that What are you importing? opened by Commodity details or Identification details saves back to the page that opened it carrying the trail, its Back opening that page.
claims.quote:
The identification page's no-commodity-line guard carries the trail on to What
are you importing?, so Back there opens the page the trader came from. What are you
importing? opened by Commodity details or Identification details saves back to the page
that opened it, carrying the trail, and its Back opens that page.

claims.statement: The journey records that a return value naming a page not allowed to open a sub-page is refused, logged and ignored.

A return value that is
not one of the pages allowed to open this sub-page is refused, logged and ignored.

claims.statement: The journey records that the county parish holding number page is the exception to the trail rules: its Back always answers the consignment addresses page carrying the trail however the page was reached, and its Save and continue answers the same page unless a required earlier answer is still missing, in which case it answers the page asking for that answer.

The county parish holding number page is the exception: its Back always answers the
consignment addresses page, carrying the trail, however the page was reached, and its
Save and continue answers the consignment addresses page as the next step that applies
— the same page, carrying the trail — unless a required earlier answer is still

claims.statement: The journey records that the Back fallback is the overview except on the first page, where it is the dashboard until an answer is entered and then the overview, and on the review, where it is the overview on a draft or an amendment and the dashboard on a submitted notification, including the one shown after an amendment is cancelled.

The fallback is the overview, except on the first
page (the dashboard until an answer is entered, then the overview: `leaveJourneyLink` in
`entry-guard.js`) and on the review (the overview on a draft or an amendment, the

claims.statement: The journey records that returning from the Import Notification Service's address book lands on a fixed address carrying no trail, and that the Consignment addresses page and Contact address for consignment are the only pages whose Back goes to the Overview whatever the trail after that return, their Save and continue still going on from them.

Returning from the Import Notification Service's address book lands on a fixed address
that carries no trail. The Consignment addresses page (the Overview task "Consignment addresses")
and Contact address for consignment (the task "Contact address
for this consignment") are the only pages whose Back goes to the Overview whatever the

claims.statement: The journey records that the hub is somewhere the user chooses to go — through the Save and return to overview button, from Overview's own address, from an Overview task, or by opening the notification from the dashboard — while Save and continue goes to the next page that applies in the journey's one page order from every start and past the last page that applies goes to the review page.
claims.quote:
The hub is somewhere the user chooses to go: through the secondary "Save and
return to overview" button on the pages that offer it
([How a page ends](page-design.md#how-a-page-ends)), from Overview's address, from an
Overview task, or by opening the notification from the dashboard.

claims.statement: The journey records that a notification is created by the dashboard's create POST or by the start entry at <set>/start, which the Import Notification Service's type question opens, through one helper that redirects to the origin page with the dashboard or the Import Notification Service as the first place on the trail.
claims.quote:
A notification is created by the dashboard's create POST or by the start entry
(`<set>/start`, which the Import Notification Service's type question opens), through one
helper in

claims.statement: The journey records that the start entry sits outside /notifications/ so the entry guard never sees it, and that the origin page is the journey entry.
claims.quote:
The start entry sits outside `/notifications/`, so the
entry guard never sees it. The origin page is the journey entry.

claims.statement: The journey records that the entry guard admits a request only when the journey carries an answer the user entered, system-populated obligations and flow-only keys such as declaration never counting as user answers, and that a journey with none is sent to the origin page, as is a request for Overview, the review, the declaration or the confirmation page, each redirect being logged once with the journey id and the requested path.
claims.quote:
The guard admits a request when the journey carries an answer the user entered.
System-populated obligations and flow-only keys such as `declaration` never count
as user answers. A journey with none (a deep link to an id this session never
created, or a draft with nothing saved) is sent to the origin page, and a request
for Overview, the review, the declaration or the confirmation page is sent there
too. Each redirect is logged once with the journey id and the requested path.

notification that cannot be found at all is answered by the guard itself with the
service's standard page not found (404), on every page, the review included,
before any page runs, and is sent nothing to the origin page or the notification
list.

The means of transport row reads the arrival page's own label for the
  stored code, so the two cannot differ.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that an answer the reference data has since retired is named on the review with the message its own page gives, and that an unfinished card says "complete" instead of the stale answer's message.
claims.quote:
An answer the reference data has since retired is named on the review with
  the message its own page gives. An unfinished card says "complete" instead
  of the stale answer's message.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that a party never answered raises no address error on the review and its card is simply unfinished.
claims.quote: A party never answered raises no address error. Its card is unfinished.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the main-import-reason card carries the exit answers and its one Change link reaches the page that collects them.
claims.quote:
The main-import-reason card carries the exit answers, and its one Change
  link reaches the page that collects them.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that a summary entry for a review card that is out of scope is absent, so every entry links to an anchor the page carries.
claims.quote:
A summary entry for a card that is out of scope is absent, so every entry
  links to an anchor the page carries.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that each review card's Change link ends, for screen readers, with the card's title in lower-case words.
claims.quote:
Each card's Change link ends, for screen readers, with the card's title in
  lower-case words.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the review's form ends with one button group and no heading or sentence stands above it, the group being Continue alone on a draft with its Delete in the header, and Continue, a secondary Cancel amend then a red Delete while amending.
claims.quote:
The review's form ends with one button group, and no heading or sentence
  stands above it. On a draft the group is Continue alone, its Delete sitting
  in the header. While amending it is Continue, a secondary Cancel amend, then
  a red Delete.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that an unfinished card's line is the same in the error summary and in the card, so a trader reading either sees the same words.
claims.quote:
An unfinished card's line is the same in the error summary and in the card,
  so a trader reading either sees the same words.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the submitted page goes from the reference panel straight to what the trader still owes, and that the declaration date is shown only on the declaration page.
claims.quote:
The page goes from the reference panel straight to what the trader still
  owes. The declaration date is shown only on the declaration page.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that documents are not required to submit, and that the submitted page lists the ITAHC as still owed unless an ITAHC is among the journey's documents, whatever its scan state.
claims.quote:
Documents are not required to submit. The page lists the ITAHC as still owed
  unless an ITAHC is among the journey's documents, whatever its scan state.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that after the ITAHC item the submitted page lists "complete the animal identifier information in the notification" when a line whose species asks for identifiers holds fewer identified animals than it declares, one filled identifier identifying an animal.
claims.quote:
After the ITAHC item, the page lists "complete the animal identifier
  information in the notification" when a line whose species asks for
  identifiers holds fewer identified animals than it declares. One filled
  identifier identifies an animal.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the submitted page's help links to HMRC open in a new tab, their visible text unchanged and a visually hidden "(opens in a new tab)" telling screen reader users.
claims.quote:
The help links to HMRC open in a new tab. Their visible text is unchanged
  and a visually hidden "(opens in a new tab)" tells screen reader users.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the customs link goes to HMRC's customs, international trade and excise enquiries page rather than its contact index, which lists every tax and helpline.
claims.quote:
The customs link goes to HMRC's customs, international trade and excise
  enquiries page, not its contact index, which lists every tax and helpline.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that "Create a new notification" is a form button styled as a link because starting a notification creates a record, and that it is offered so a trader with a second consignment need not return to the dashboard to find the start button.
claims.quote:
"Create a new notification" is a form button styled as a link, because
  starting a notification creates a record. It is offered so a trader with a
  second consignment need not return to the dashboard to find the start
  button.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the declaration's confirmation is one small checkbox in a fieldset whose legend is for screen readers only, so a lone checkbox still has a group label.
claims.quote:
The confirmation is one small checkbox in a fieldset whose legend is for
  screen readers only, so a lone checkbox still has a group label.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the declaration page carries no status strip, at a first submission or an amendment.
claims.quote: The page carries no status strip, at a first submission or an amendment.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the date of declaration is shown in bold.
claims.quote: The date of declaration is shown in bold.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that a hidden step field tells a Submit from a Continue on the declaration, because an unticked box posts nothing.
claims.quote:
The hidden `step` tells a Submit from a Continue, because an unticked box
  posts nothing.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the declaration checkbox is never pre-ticked, because a tick left by a submit refused as stale was given to older content.
claims.quote:
The checkbox is never pre-ticked, because a tick left by a submit refused
  as stale was given to older content.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the country of origin is required on save and continue, an empty answer being refused with "Select a country of origin", a typed value not in the list with "Select a country from the list", and a saved country the reference data no longer offers being refused on submit with its own message.
claims.quote:
The country is required on save and continue. An empty answer is refused with
  **Select a country of origin**; a typed value not in the list is refused with
  **Select a country from the list**. A saved country the reference data no
  longer offers is refused on submit with its own message.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the country of origin list names a territory with its country, as in "Canary Islands (Spain)", and is sorted by the name shown.
claims.quote:
The list names a territory with its country, "Canary Islands (Spain)", and
  is sorted by the name shown.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that with JavaScript the region code box shows the country's code as a fixed prefix, empty until a country is picked and filled in as soon as one is so the trader types only the rest, that without JavaScript there is no prefix, and that the stored answer is the whole joined code either way.
claims.quote:
With JavaScript the region code box shows the country's code as a fixed
  prefix, empty until a country is picked and filled in as soon as one is, so
  the trader types only the rest. Without JavaScript there is no prefix. The
  stored answer is the whole joined code either way.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the server always draws the region code prefix so a revisit or an error shows the saved or submitted code at once, styling hiding it until GOV.UK Frontend's JavaScript can run and a small client module updating it on a change of country.
claims.quote:
The server always draws the prefix, so a revisit or an error shows the saved
  or submitted code at once. Styling hides it until GOV.UK Frontend's
  JavaScript can run, and a small client module updates it on a change of
  country.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the country-to-prefix rule has one owner on the server, the page handing the browser a map built with it and the client module only looking the chosen country up.
claims.quote:
The country-to-prefix rule has one owner on the server. The page hands the
  browser a map built with it, and the module only looks the chosen country up.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that a region code typed with the country's code and a hyphen, such as FR-75, is recognised and not doubled, while a code typed with the country's letters but no hyphen, such as FR75, is kept as typed and joined to the prefix as FR-FR75, because a real region code can begin with those letters.
claims.quote:
A code typed with the country's code and a hyphen (for example "FR-75") is
  recognised and not doubled. A code typed with the country's letters but no
  hyphen (for example "FR75") is kept as typed and joined to the prefix
  ("FR-FR75"), because a real region code can begin with those letters.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the region code is required under Yes and stored only with a country's prefix, and that under No, or with no country, the stored code is empty.
claims.quote:
The region code is required under Yes, and stored only with a country's
  prefix. Under No, or with no country, the stored code is empty.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the region code rules measure the typed part with any typed prefix removed, whatever the answer, while the page shows back what was typed.
claims.quote:
The rules measure the typed part with any typed prefix removed, whatever the
  answer; the page shows back what was typed.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the region code box stops typing at the same length the rule allows, the stop applying to the raw text, so a trader without JavaScript who types the country's code before a rest of more than two characters has it cut short.
claims.quote:
The region code box stops typing at the same length the rule allows. The
  stop applies to the raw text, so a trader without JavaScript who types the
  country's code before a rest of more than two characters has it cut short.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that clearing the country clears the region code too, because the prefix depends on the country.
claims.quote:
Clearing the country clears the region code too, because the prefix
  depends on the country.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the internal reference is checked for length only, being the trader's own and keeping their punctuation.
claims.quote:
The internal reference is checked for length only. It is the trader's own
  and keeps their punctuation.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the origin page's status strip shows from the first request.
claims.quote: The status strip shows from the first request.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that stored answers are re-checked against the origin page's rules when the page opens, so a country the reference data no longer offers is named on the page.
claims.quote:
Stored answers are re-checked against the page's rules when the page opens,
  so a country the reference data no longer offers is named on the page.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the Overview origin task reads Complete only when a country is chosen and the region of origin code question is answered, Yes with a code or No.
claims.quote:
The overview origin task reads Complete only when a country is chosen and
  the region of origin code question is answered (Yes with a code, or No).

claims.statement: The page-design record states that a question two import reasons ask has a form field per reason because two inputs cannot share a name, both mapping back to the one answer.
claims.quote:
A question two reasons ask has a form field per reason, because two inputs
  cannot share a name. Both map back to the one answer.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the reason a reveal belongs to carries the explanation, so its follow-up questions ask with a label alone and the exit date keeps only its worked example.
claims.quote:
The reason a reveal belongs to carries the explanation, so its follow-up
  questions ask with a label alone, and the exit date keeps only its worked
  example.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the unreadable-date message does not repeat the field name the label already gives.
claims.quote:
The unreadable-date message does not repeat the field name that the label
  already gives.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the destination country and port of exit are type-ahead searches using the shared search control, with the look the origin and port of entry searches share: a bold label and full width.
claims.quote:
The destination country and port of exit are type-ahead searches using the
  shared search control, with the look the origin and port of entry searches
  share: a bold label and full width.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that type-ahead suggestions match ignoring accents as well as case, so plain letters find "Côte d'Ivoire".
claims.quote:
Type-ahead suggestions match ignoring accents as well as case, so plain
  letters find "Côte d'Ivoire".

claims.statement: The page-design record states that origin and port of entry share the medium label while the main import reason page asks its searches as follow-up questions, so it sets the small label itself and "Select one" in both the empty box and the select's first option.
claims.quote:
Origin and port of entry share the medium label, but this page asks its
  searches as follow-up questions, so it sets the small label itself, and
  "Select one" in both the empty box and the select's first option.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the exit date has a regular-weight label and a GOV.UK margin override on its form group, because GOV.UK Frontend zeroes the bottom margin of the last form group nested in another, which would leave the date box touching "Port of exit".
claims.quote:
The exit date has a regular-weight label and a GOV.UK margin override on its
  form group. GOV.UK Frontend zeroes
  the bottom margin of the last form group nested in another, which would leave
  the date box touching "Port of exit".

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the additional details page's certification hint names the ITAHC because a trader holds several certificates so "the health certificate" does not say which one the certification purposes are copied from, the abbreviation matching the documents and review pages.
claims.quote:
The certification hint names the ITAHC because a trader holds several
  certificates, so "the health certificate" does not say which one the
  certification purposes are copied from. The abbreviation matches the
  documents and review pages.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the identification page uses the full-width surface so the tables and cards fit, while the error summary, caption, heading and inset text keep a two-thirds reading width.
claims.quote:
The page uses the full-width surface so the tables and cards fit. The error
  summary, caption, heading and inset text keep a two-thirds reading width.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that identification is grouped by commodity, one section per commodity headed "<commodity name> (<commodity code>)" holding one card per species.
claims.quote:
Identification is grouped by commodity: one section per commodity headed
  "<commodity name> (<commodity code>)", holding one card per species.

claims.statement: The page-design record states the decision that the identification card is built from GOV.UK summary card styling and govukTable rather than the prototype's custom CSS and div grid, so tables keep their meaning and reflow at 390px.
claims.quote:
The
  card is built from GOV.UK summary card styling and `govukTable`, not the
  prototype's custom CSS and div grid, so tables keep their meaning and
  reflow at 390px.
claims.note: A recorded departure from the prototype's implementation, kept for accessibility and reflow rather than appearance.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the saved-animals and Selected commodities tables set a deliberate custom class on their cells so long unbroken identifiers and commodity names wrap inside table cells at 390px.
claims.quote:
The saved-animals and Selected commodities tables set
  `app-table__cell--break-anywhere` on their cells. It is a deliberate custom
  class so long unbroken identifiers and commodity names wrap inside table
  cells at 390px.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that a species with no number of animals has no identification card, and a consignment whose species all lack a count shows the summary and no cards.
claims.quote:
A species with no number of animals has no card, and a consignment whose
  species all lack a count shows the summary and no cards.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the identification card title is the species name with "Change number of animals" beside it naming the species, and that the link pushes the identification page onto the trail so Back on the count page returns there and Continue on Commodity details goes on to the next page that applies.
claims.quote:
The card title is the species name, with "Change number of animals" beside
  it naming the species. The link pushes this page onto the trail, so Back on the count page returns here and Continue on
  Commodity details goes on to the next page that applies.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that while animals remain the identification card shows the entry form, then the in-card button, then the saved-animals table, that a finished species shows its saved animals alone with no form, no button and no completion message, and that a count lowered below its saved records still shows the over-count message.
claims.quote:
While animals remain the card shows the entry form, then the in-card button,
  then the saved-animals table. A finished species shows its saved animals
  alone, with no form, no button and no completion message. A count lowered
  below its saved records still shows the over-count message.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the identification in-card button says what pressing it does next, reading "Save and add another" while more than one animal is outstanding and "Save and finish" on the last, is a primary button, saves only its own species' current animal and reloads with that form empty, and that a line of one animal has no in-card button.
claims.quote:
The in-card button says what pressing it does next: "Save and add another"
  while more than one animal is outstanding, "Save and finish" on the last,
  and it is a primary button. It saves only its own species' current animal
  and reloads with that form empty. A line of one animal has no in-card
  button.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that on the identification page "Save and continue" and "Save and return to overview" save only the forms of species with one animal, values typed into the form of a species with more animals being neither validated nor saved by them.
claims.quote:
"Save and continue" and "Save and return to overview"
  save only the forms of species with one animal. Values typed into the form
  of a species with more animals are neither validated nor saved by them.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that pressing Enter in any identification field presses the page's hidden default button, which saves every card holding typed values including species with more animals and keeps the trader on the page when one of those was saved, the hidden button coming first in the form so Enter never presses a Remove button or the visible "Save and continue".
claims.quote:
Pressing Enter in any field presses the page's hidden default button. It
  saves every card holding typed values, species with more animals included,
  and keeps the trader on the page when one of those was saved. The hidden
  button comes first in the form so that Enter never presses a Remove button
  or the visible "Save and continue".

claims.statement: The page-design record states that an identifier has one name used both on the entry field and as the saved-animals column heading, that no identifier field has a hint, and that the labels are regular weight.
claims.quote:
An identifier has one name, used both on the entry field and as the
  saved-animals column heading, and no identifier field has a hint. Labels
  are regular weight.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the saved-animals table has one column per identifier that species' panel asks for rather than per identifier the trader filled — the commodity's own identifiers, or the two free-text fallback answers for a commodity that declares none — so the header row says which identifiers the line expects and an empty cell shows which are still missing.
claims.quote:
The saved-animals table has one column per identifier that species' panel
  asks for, not per identifier the trader filled: the commodity's own
  identifiers, or the two free-text fallback answers for a commodity that
  declares none. The header row says which identifiers the line expects, and
  an empty cell shows which are still missing.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that removing an identifier record is a POST on the card form with no GET, so a link cannot trigger it.
claims.quote:
Removing an identifier record is a POST on the card form with no GET, so a
  link cannot trigger it.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the identification page is skipped only when the notification holds no commodity line.
claims.quote: The page is skipped only when the notification holds no commodity line.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that on the commodity pages a choice made under an earlier search has no tick box on screen, so it is sent back with the form as a hidden value.
claims.quote:
A choice made under an earlier search has no tick box on screen, so it is
  sent back with the form as a hidden value.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that with JavaScript the commodity search results refresh in place as the trader types, ticks, removes or clears, through the shared multi-select search, and that the results are the ones the page renders without JavaScript so the ordering, labelling and selection rules hold on both paths.
claims.quote:
With JavaScript the results refresh in place as the trader types, ticks,
  removes or clears, through the shared multi-select search. The results are
  the ones the page renders without JavaScript, so the ordering, labelling and
  selection rules below hold on both paths.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that a polite status message gives the number of species a typed commodity search lists, or "No results found", and that a tick, a Remove or Clear all is not announced because the box and the tally already show it.
claims.quote:
A polite status message gives the number of species a typed
  search lists, or "No results found". A tick, a Remove or Clear all is not
  announced, because the box and the tally already show it.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that after a Remove or Clear all on the commodity search the button pressed has gone so focus moves to the search box, while after a tick focus stays on the tick box.
claims.quote:
After a Remove or Clear all, the button pressed has gone, so focus moves to
  the search box. After a tick, focus stays on the tick box.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that without JavaScript a tick cannot refresh the tally so an "Add selection" secondary button sits under the commodity results, running the search again keeping the term and the ticks so the tally catches up, and that with JavaScript the button is hidden.
claims.quote:
Without JavaScript a tick cannot refresh the tally, so an "Add selection"
  secondary button sits under the results. It runs the search again, keeping
  the term and the ticks, and the tally catches up. With JavaScript
  the button is hidden, because a tick refreshes the tally itself.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the "Add selection" button and its copy are agreed for now and will be revisited when the designers pick up their no-JavaScript ticket.
claims.quote:
The button and
  its copy are agreed for now, and will be revisited when the designers pick
  up their no-JavaScript ticket.
claims.note: The only place the repo records a piece of English copy as provisionally agreed and awaiting a design decision.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the commodity search results are a list joined to the bottom of the search box as the design draws it: one heading row per commodity with its species beneath, striped rows ruled the full width of the list with the first species under each heading shaded, no ring round a hovered tick box, and a scroll once the list is taller than about six rows.
claims.quote:
The results are a list joined to the bottom of the search box, as the
  design draws it: one heading row per commodity, its species beneath, striped
  rows ruled the full width of the list (the first species under each heading
  shaded), no ring round a hovered tick box, and a scroll once the list is taller
  than about six rows.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that each commodity in the search results stays a fieldset whose legend is its heading, so a screen reader hears the species grouped by commodity.
claims.quote:
Each commodity stays a fieldset whose legend is its
  heading, so a screen reader hears the species grouped by commodity.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that a commodity's heading in the results and in the tally reads as its name with its code in round brackets, such as "Cattle (0102)", where the service knows a name for the code, and as the code alone where it does not, while the Commodity details page still names a commodity by its code.
claims.quote:
A commodity's heading in the results, and in the tally, reads as
  its name with its code in round brackets, such as "Cattle (0102)", where the
  service knows a name for the code, and as the code alone where it does not.
  The names come from `commodityNameFor` in the set's commodities service; the
  Commodity details page still names a commodity by its code.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that with JavaScript, Escape in the commodity search box or a click outside the search hides the list while keeping the term and every choice, focusing or clicking the search box showing it again, and that the list hides once the click has landed so a click on a button below the list is not moved out from under the pointer.
claims.quote:
With JavaScript, Escape in the search box or a click outside the search hides
  the list, keeping the term and every choice, and focusing or clicking the
  search box shows it again. The list hides once the click has landed, so a
  click on a button below the list is not moved out from under the pointer.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the commodity tally, the panel of what has been chosen, shows a chip per species under its commodity's heading as the design draws it, the species' Latin name and a cross named "Remove" and that Latin name, with Clear all beside the count as a form button styled as a link that posts the page form.
claims.quote:
The tally, the panel of what has been chosen, shows a chip per species,
  under its commodity's heading,
  as the design draws it: the species' Latin name and a cross named "Remove"
  and that Latin name. Clear all sits beside the count, as a form
  button styled as a link that posts the page form.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that if the commodity search results cannot be fetched the page is posted as it is without JavaScript, so the trader still gets the results.
claims.quote:
If the results cannot be fetched, the page is posted as it is without
  JavaScript, so the trader still gets the results.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that one commodity search result is announced as "1 result available" while the design announces "1 results available", the singular being open with the designer.
claims.quote:
One result is announced as "1 result available". The design announces
  "1 results available"; the singular is open with the designer.
claims.note: A recorded open design question against the design source's own wording.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that a commodity search's results are listed in order, the commodity groups by their code and each group's species by the label they are offered under, over the page of results the search returned.
claims.quote:
A search's results are listed in order: the commodity groups by their
  code, and each group's species by the label they are offered under, over
  the page of results the search returned.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that a species reads as its Latin name with its common name in round brackets wherever it is listed or named — the search results, Commodity details, the Selected commodities tables and Identification details, but not the tally's chips, which the design gives the Latin name alone — and as its Latin name alone where the reference data holds no common name for it.
claims.quote:
A species reads as its Latin name with its common name in round
  brackets wherever it is listed or named — the search results, Commodity
  details, the Selected commodities tables and Identification details, but
  not the tally's chips, which the design gives the Latin name
  alone — and as its Latin name alone where the
  reference data holds no common name for it.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the permanent-address rule and the identifier-column rule read the line's stored Latin name rather than the displayed species label, so a species whose common name changes what it reads as still gates the same way.
claims.quote:
The permanent-address rule and the identifier-column rule read the line's stored Latin name rather
  than that label, so a species whose common name changes what it reads as
  still gates the same way.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the commodity tally offers a removal per chosen species, posting the page form with the species' key in the button value so the entry pressed is the entry removed however the panel is ordered.
claims.quote:
The tally offers a removal per chosen species, posting the page
  form with the species' key in the button value so the entry pressed is the
  entry removed however the panel is ordered

claims.statement: The page-design record states that because a tick box on screen carries no hidden value, a removal naming a choice the post no longer carries, the trader having unticked that box first, is honoured and nothing is logged.
claims.quote:
Because a tick box on screen carries no hidden value, a removal naming a
  choice the post no longer carries, because the trader unticked that box
  first, is honoured and nothing is logged.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that a removal naming a key the stored search rows never held is refused with a bad request and one logged refusal, reachable by a tampered post and by a page left open across a save and a later removal of that commodity line on commodity details, because a save empties the stored search rows.
claims.quote:
A removal naming a key the stored
  search rows never held is refused with a bad request and one logged
  refusal — reachable by a tampered post, and by a page left open across a
  save and a later removal of that commodity line on commodity details,
  because a save empties the stored search rows.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that commodity code 01061900 covers several commodities and hundreds of species, and that each chosen species gets its own Selected commodities row named by the species on both Commodity details and Identification.
claims.quote:
Commodity code 01061900 covers several commodities and hundreds of species.
  Each chosen species gets its own Selected commodities row, named by the
  species, on both Commodity details and Identification.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the commodity heading on Commodity details is set at the larger size because the commodity blocks are the substance of the page, the type stepping down from commodity to species to quantity labels, and the labels carrying a size so they do not read at the weight of their hints.
claims.quote:
The commodity heading on Commodity details is set at the larger size because
  the commodity blocks are the substance of the page. The type steps down from
  commodity to species to quantity labels, and the labels carry a size so they
  do not read at the weight of their hints.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the number of animals question has no hint because the page repeats it per species, so an example would repeat with it.
claims.quote:
The number of animals question has no hint because the page repeats it per
  species, so an example would repeat with it.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that a commodity search option shows the species label with the part the query matched in bold, so a trader can see at a glance why each result was offered.
claims.quote:
A search option shows the species label with the part the query matched in
  bold, so a trader can see at a glance why each result was offered.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the commodity inset's second sentence stops a reader concluding that goods with no certificate need no notification.
claims.quote:

fixed startup cost that does not shrink for a small change. Charging that to
every commit — including the ones you are about to squash — is what teaches
people to reach for `--no-verify`, which skips the cheap format and lint
checks as well. A push is the first point the work affects anyone else, so
the gate sits there.
